correctness.rationale: The proof uses the exact Alexander-polynomial formulas printed in Kegel--Schmalian. Their exponent-order analysis shows all thirteen terms are distinct for |m|>=3 and for n>=4 or n<=-5, so the coefficient of magnitude seven survives in every infinite-range case. Exact expansion of the eleven exceptional parameters gives maxima 7,13,9,7 for K and 7,7,5,13,9,7,7 for J. The standard Ozsvath--Szabo consequence for an L-space knot requires every nonzero Alexander coefficient to have absolute value one. Therefore every nonzero family member is excluded.

value.rationale: The recent paper places L-space knots and its explicit multiple-surgery families on opposite sides of the strongly-characterising-slope discussion: hyperbolic L-space knots have a positive uniqueness theorem, while the L9a20 families provide systematic non-uniqueness. Determining that every nonzero member of both negative-example families lies outside the L-space-knot class is therefore a motivated structural classification, not an arbitrary coefficient check. It identifies a clean boundary for applying L-space Floer machinery to these examples and is complete over all integer parameters.
